# Vendor integration and verification

Verified against live official documentation on 2026-09-22 using the explicitly invoked [TypeSafe skill](../../SKILL.md) and OpenAI Docs skill. No authenticated inference request was made; tests inject mocked HTTP responses and credentials.

- [TypeSafe HTTP API](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api.md), [Choice](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/choice.md), [Noul](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/noul.md), [state](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/state.md), and the [hierarchical-classification cookbook](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/hierarchical_classification.md): a request contains named state and keyed questions; one Choice supplies relative probabilities/certainty and independent Nouls supply absolute yes probabilities. The cookbook's hierarchical search is not used: this design sends all defined types together. Question IDs are identifiers, so each question explicitly references the state fields and contains the full type definition. The versioned model remains jev-1.13.0.
- [Responses create](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/cli/resources/responses/methods/create), [structured outputs](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs), [Batch](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/batch), [Terra](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-terra), and [Luna](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-luna): Responses uses strict text.format JSON schema; explicit max_output_tokens, store=false and truncation=disabled are included. Batch wraps the exact interactive body under a unique custom_id.

`requests.ts` exports immutable request builders, response decoders, `verifyModelPolicy`, Batch JSONL construction and complete-result validation. `FrozenVendorRequest` includes the immutable modelPolicy as well as body bytes. Per the owner's explicit exception to the original design, only approved gpt-5.6-terra/gpt-5.6-luna aliases can accept their exact bare name or a same-family dated snapshot. Other families fail. The actual returned model is preserved in raw records, normalized results and call logs. Existing strict normalized validators remain unchanged: the adapter checks the authorized family first, then validates against that verified actual ID.

`executeVendor(request, policy, dependencies, decode)` invokes only injected fetch. Dependencies supply persistent guard checks (live-call gate, kill switch and budget), secret lookup, immutable R2 persistence, D1 call/usage rows, durable per-vendor failure counters, clock, unique attempt IDs and sleep. The integration must bound fetch timeouts, persist all failure events and prevent Workflow retries from restarting this whole bounded loop. Map reader/recovery circuit outcomes to their shared vendor.

Raw response body and metadata are persisted before JSON parsing; failures to persist or log halt. Tokens and returned model are logged without credentials. Missing usage on a valid successful JSON response halts because live spend cannot be omitted silently. Network failures record a typed fact, with no potentially sensitive exception text. Guard runs before every attempt and again after response logging. Any returned model outside policy halts even on retryable HTTP errors. Three transport attempts are permitted; only the reader gets one identical schema retry, with at most six requests overall. Recovery/ confidence accept one schema attempt. Every attempt gets a new artifact key. Retry-after takes precedence over the capped exponential backoff, including HTTP dates; malformed headers fail visibly. The adapter never edits prompts, request bytes, evidence or outputs during retries.

After storing a complete raw Batch output/error file, call `parseBatchResults` with the full expected ID set. Missing, duplicate or unrelated IDs are blockers; per-item errors remain explicit. Batch lifecycle polling/submission and use of the same decoder are integration responsibilities. Outline recovery output still requires `verifyRecoveredHeadings`; the model only locates lines and no recovered heading is accepted without local exact-text verification.

## Batch lifecycle

`batch.ts` adds `validateBatchInput`, `uploadBatchInput`, `createBatch`, `pollBatch`, and `ingestBatchResults`. Each accepts explicit run/batch/model context and injected persistence/auth/guard/fetch dependencies. Upload uses streamed multipart Files purpose=batch, then POST /v1/batches uses /v1/responses and completion_window=24h. Polling is one GET per call; the orchestrator schedules the next poll and persists state via persistBatchState. Upload/create are never retried automatically: an uncertain POST response could already have created a remote object. Reconcile the persisted raw response/request event before any new submission.

The official [Batch guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/batch), rechecked 2026-09-22, specifies 50,000 requests and 200 MB per input file, and separate account queued-token limits. The helper enforces 50,000 and conservatively treats MB as decimal (200,000,000 UTF-8 bytes). It does not assume an account queue allowance; preflight must check the configured allowance. Multipart upload captures immutable request bytes, streams one JSONL line at a time and adds no model parameters. Output/error files are streamed as raw immutable byte chunks before UTF-8 decoding or JSON parsing. Memory retains at most one result line plus the configured chunk and correlation IDs/references, not a whole 200 MB file. Explicit I/O policy must stay within metadata 16 MiB, result line 32 MiB and chunk 1 MiB safety bounds; a typical configuration is 1 MiB / 8 MiB / 64 KiB. These are visible processing failures, never truncation.

`persistChunk` receives retrievalId/fileId/index/bytes; metadata responses use fileId=metadata. `stageResult` must persist an immutable record and return its reference WITHOUT deciding the document. Only after correlation finishes may the caller process returned result references. Missing/duplicate results become explicit per-document failures; unknown IDs, malformed JSON, model drift or interrupted streams halt ingestion. Output/error vendor failures are retained. Expired/cancelled/failed batches never silently lose unfinished documents. The return's correlationComplete flag means every expected identifier has a result or a failure; it does not claim all documents succeeded. Persist these final outcomes in D1 before completing the run.

A reader schema retry may be a new Batch containing precisely the same frozen request body, within the original run's one permitted schema retry and recorded attempt budget. These helpers never resubmit failed documents or choose retry candidates themselves. Files remain until explicit user run closure; integration is responsible for remote input-file cleanup on closure and must not add expiration timers. Kill/live/budget guards execute before every network operation and while consuming response streams. No live API calls were made during implementation.

### Cache controls

Reader/recovery now set prompt_cache_options.mode=explicit and no prompt_cache_breakpoint markers. Official Responses documentation says this removes the implicit cache breakpoint, and explicit-only cache lookup checks only explicit breakpoints. Thus these single-turn requests select no cached prefix. This transport option does not change model-visible content. The no-cache policy was chosen during the owner-authorized spending review on 2026-09-22 to avoid the GPT-5.6 cache-write premium and discount accounting ambiguity. `actualUsageCost` requires explicit zero read/write cache counters; unexpected cached usage blocks accounting rather than silently treating it at ordinary rates. See the cost README for official source links and integration requirements.

### Backend Batch grouping and accounting

The server plans groups from immutable R2 artifact HEAD sizes in checkpointed sets of 50; it does not load every full-text request to measure a run. Groups retain at most 8 MiB of request artifacts, with a single larger artifact up to 32 MiB isolated in its own group. Only the current group is loaded. This changes transport grouping only; exact request bytes and classification inputs remain unchanged. Group/schema identifiers are present in every lifecycle stage name and batch key. The original group's first document supplies the batch_jobs fingerprint key, preserving the existing unique constraint without a migration.

Schema retry identifiers are read back from the persisted validation artifact, so replay does not depend on a callback repopulating an in-memory array. Every result line receives its own immutable raw artifact and staging event; usage accounting is inserted once per batch key/custom ID, allowing duplicate correlation to produce an explicit failure without duplicate billing. Actual usage validation runs with the disabled-cache policy; raw data and a null-cost call row are persisted before an accounting blocker is propagated.

Explicit run closure cleanup (2026-09-22): `cancelAndDeleteBatchInputs` uses durable input-file IDs only, retrieves each Batch, cancels active work, and returns pending until the vendor confirms a terminal status. The caller must not finish closure or claim text removed while pending. It then deletes only Batch input files; vendor outputs and local raw audit artifacts are retained. There is no inference/live-budget guard on user-authorized cleanup and no automatic retry. Each control response is persisted before parsing; uncertain operations remain blockers for reconciliation. Caller omits already-deleted IDs using its cleanup ledger. Unknown/mismatched IDs and non-success deletion responses remain blockers (a 404 is not silently converted into a successful deletion receipt). Control responses have a 1 MiB bound.

Batch result accounting distinguishes unsuccessful requests without reported usage from successful requests with missing usage. Non-success results retain `cost_nano: null` and an explicit `unsuccessful_no_usage` audit disposition, allowing per-document failure correlation. This is not a fabricated zero-cost usage measurement. Successful missing usage still blocks; any reported usage is validated and accounted. Batch per-request latency is null because no measured individual inference duration is available.

Verified official references: https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/batches/methods/cancel (cancellation can remain cancelling before becoming cancelled); https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/files/methods/delete (DELETE file returns id and deleted); https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/batch (expired requests are unexecuted; completed work is billed). No live vendor calls were made.
